purpose: Offline comparison of adaptive, stateless-role, and fixed-cycle search policies across synthetic v2 scheduling scenarios.

scenarios.description: Denser recurrence of the existing special cohorts.

target_promotion.reason: Strongest medium gain in all three scenarios.
target_promotion.protocol: one worker, seed 101, 120 seconds total, 30 seconds per operator, full validation
target_promotion.stopping_observation: Both operator attempts returned UNKNOWN without a strict improvement; target optimality is unresolved.

protocol.validation_budget_adjustment: Target-scale full-model validation measured approximately 89-100 seconds; the original 60-second operator/validation budget could not authoritatively classify candidates, so the long-horizon gate used 180 seconds for each.
protocol.target_seed101_gate: 600 seconds total, 180 seconds per operator, 180 seconds validation, one CP-SAT worker, supervised 720-second parent wall
protocol.candidate_validation_observation: No target candidate was validated or adopted. Most probes returned UNKNOWN; several final attempts reached candidate_validation_error after the operator consumed its search budget. The retained Stage 1 seed is authoritative and complete, but target substantive optimality remains unresolved.

scenario_selection.reason: Promoted matched analogues after fixed-cycle was strongest in all three medium scenario families across seeds 101, 202, and 303.
scenario_selection.dense_special_target_stage1_validation_n: The 1,400-student dense-special seed required the longer validation allowance; the earlier 30-second validation failure was not a feasibility result.
